domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, manager decision, and potential cancellation. The status field drives all workflow gating.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers; editable by the employee
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted for manager review; locked for employee edits; visible to the manager
APPROVED — manager has approved the request; balance has been deducted; employee may cancel from this state
REJECTED — manager has rejected the request; terminal state; no balance impact
CANCELLED — request was cancelled by the employee; terminal state; if cancelled from APPROVED, balance is restored

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestTransitions
domain_entities.purpose: Documents every valid state transition for LeaveRequest. Each transition is a named operation that the domain service must enforce. No transition outside this set is valid.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (submit) — employee finalises and submits the request; triggers manager notification
SUBMITTED → APPROVED (approve) — manager approves; balance is deducted; approvedBy and approvedAt are set
SUBMITTED → REJECTED (reject) — manager rejects; no balance impact; terminal
SUBMITTED → DRAFT (withdraw) — employee withdraws the submission back to draft for editing
APPROVED → CANCELLED (cancel) — employee cancels an approved leave; balance is restored
DRAFT → CANCELLED (cancelDraft) — employee discards a draft; terminal

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Drives sufficiency checks during leave application and is mutated on approval and cancellation.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect for the current fiscal year; accruals and deductions apply
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays has reached zero; no further leave of this type can be taken until accrual or new fiscal year
CLOSED — fiscal year has ended; balance is archived; a new balance record is created for the next fiscal year

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a category of leave. Drives balance initialisation, sufficiency checks, notice-period validation, and whether manager approval is required. One policy per leave type per organisation context.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; employees can apply for leave under this policy; accruals run
INACTIVE — policy is suspended; no new applications accepted; existing approved leaves are unaffected
ARCHIVED — policy is retired; no longer visible for new applications; historical data preserved

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. The employmentStatus gates eligibility for leave applications. The managerId establishes the approval chain for submitted leave requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — employee is currently employed; eligible for leave applications
INACTIVE — employee is on extended leave or suspended; leave applications may be restricted
TERMINATED — employment has ended; no leave applications allowed; historical balances preserved

business_rules: Leave day count is computed as calendar days inclusive: daysRequested = (endDate - startDate) + 1. A leave from Monday to Friday consumes 5 days. This count is used for balance deduction, sufficiency checks, and balance restoration. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest day counting appears, not only here]
An employee may only submit a leave request if their employmentStatus is ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

startDate must be on or after the current date. Backdated leave requests are not permitted through the employee self-service flow. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]
endDate must be on or after startDate. A zero-day or negative-duration leave request is invalid. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

If the associated LeavePolicy has a minimumNoticeDays value, then (startDate - today) must be >= minimumNoticeDays. The notice period is computed as calendar days, inclusive of today. If minimumNoticeDays is undefined or 0, no notice constraint applies. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission — notice period appears, not only here]

On approval, the system must verify that the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and fiscal year has remainingDays >= daysRequested. If insufficient, approval must be rejected with a clear insufficiency reason. The fiscal year is derived from startDate: if startDate month >= fiscal year start month (default January), fiscalYear = startDate year; otherwise fiscalYear = startDate year - 1. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — balance sufficiency appears, not only here]

On approval, the employee's LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by daysRequested, and remainingDays is decremented by the same amount. If remainingDays reaches 0, the balance status transitions to EXHAUSTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — balance deduction appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest is cancelled from APPROVED state, the employee's LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by daysRequested, and remainingDays is incremented by the same amount. If the balance was EXHAUSTED, it returns to ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation — balance restoration appears, not only here]

Only the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a submitted leave request. If the employee has no manager (managerId is null), the request is escalated to an HR admin role. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — manager authorisation appears, not only here]

If the LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is false, the leave request transitions directly from SUBMITTED to APPROVED without manager intervention, provided the balance sufficiency check passes. No approvedBy or approvedAt is set in this case. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — auto-approval appears, not only here]

Each employee has exactly one LeaveBalance record per policy per fiscal year. When a leave request spans a fiscal year boundary (startDate and endDate fall in different fiscal years), the request must be split or rejected — a single LeaveRequest cannot draw from two fiscal year balances. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance — fiscal year scoping appears, not only here]

The associated LeavePolicy must be ACTIVE at the time of submission. A request referencing an INACTIVE or ARCHIVED policy must be rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission — policy active check appears, not only here]

Only the owning employee may create, edit, submit, withdraw, or cancel their own leave request. Managers may only approve or reject. HR admins may perform any action as an override. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest — employee ownership appears, not only here]

When an employee's employmentStatus transitions to TERMINATED, all of their SUBMITTED (pending) leave requests are automatically cancelled. APPROVED leave requests with future dates are also cancelled and balances restored. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Employee status change — pending leave requests appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

### LeaveRequest
- DRAFT → SUBMITTED → {APPROVED | REJECTED}
- SUBMITTED → DRAFT (withdraw)
- APPROVED → CANCELLED
- DRAFT → CANCELLED
- Terminal states: REJECTED, CANCELLED

### LeaveBalance
- ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (when remainingDays reaches 0)
- EXHAUSTED → ACTIVE (when balance is restored via cancellation)
- ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED → CLOSED (fiscal year end)
- Terminal state: CLOSED

### LeavePolicy
- ACTIVE → INACTIVE → ARCHIVED
- INACTIVE → ACTIVE (reactivation)
- Terminal state: ARCHIVED

### Employee
- ACTIVE → INACTIVE → TERMINATED
- INACTIVE → ACTIVE (reactivation)
- Terminal state: TERMINATED

## Key domain decisions

1. Day counting is inclusive calendar days: (endDate - startDate) + 1. This is a broad rule applied everywhere — balance deduction, sufficiency checks, and restoration.
2. Fiscal year is derived from startDate using January as default start month (open question on configurability).
3. Cross-fiscal-year leave requests are rejected — a single request cannot span two fiscal years.
4. Auto-approval when LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is false.
5. Employee termination cascades to cancel all pending and future approved leave requests with balance restoration.
6. Managerless employees have their requests escalated to HR admin for approval.
7. Only ACTIVE employees may submit leave; only ACTIVE policies may be used.

## Open questions for chief architect
- Fiscal year start month (January vs configurable)
- Overlapping leave request policy (reject vs allow)
- Half-day leave support (full-day only vs half-day flags vs DateTime)

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal year start month? The domain currently assumes January (calendar year). Many organisations use April or July. This affects which fiscalYear a leave request maps to for balance lookups.
open_questions.impact: Affects balance sufficiency checks and fiscal year derivation logic in LeaveBalance lookup. If wrong, leave requests could be checked against the wrong year's balance.
candidate_options: Configurable per organisation — store in a tenant/organisation settings entity

open_questions.question: Should the system prevent overlapping leave requests for the same employee? If so, what states count as "active" for overlap detection (APPROVED only, or SUBMITTED + APPROVED)?
open_questions.impact: Affects submission validation logic. Without this rule, an employee could book annual leave and sick leave for the same dates, potentially double-consuming balance or creating scheduling conflicts.
candidate_options: Reject overlapping requests — an employee cannot have two APPROVED or SUBMITTED leave requests with overlapping date ranges
Allow overlapping requests — different leave types can overlap (e.g. sick leave during annual leave)
Allow overlap only for specific leave types (e.g. sick and emergency can overlap with annual)

open_questions.question: Should the system support half-day leave requests? The current model uses Date for startDate/endDate, implying full-day granularity.
open_questions.impact: Affects the day-counting formula (BR on inclusive calendar days would need to account for 0.5-day increments) and the LeaveRequest schema.
candidate_options: Full-day only — startDate and endDate are date-only; no half-day support
Half-day support via a halfDayStart and halfDayEnd boolean flags on LeaveRequest
Half-day support via time component on startDate/endDate (switch from Date to DateTime)
